2026-05-01.text:
Spent the morning touring Hearst Castle's guesthouses, Neptune Pool, and Casa Grande, then drove down the coast to watch elephant seals and pelicans at Piedras Blancas — sunshine throughout, crowds light.

**Highlights:**

- [Hearst Castle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hearst_Castle) — hilltop estate built for William Randolph Hearst beginning in 1919, designed by architect Julia Morgan in Mediterranean Revival style
- [Neptune Pool](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neptune_Pool) — outdoor pool featuring a reconstructed Roman temple façade; holds approximately 345,000 gallons
- [Casa Grande](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Casa_Grande_(Hearst_Castle)) — main house anchored by twin Celestial Towers modeled on a Spanish cathedral façade
- [Piedras Blancas elephant seal rookery](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Piedras_Blancas_elephant_seal_rookery) — established in 1990, now home to over 17,000 northern elephant seals
- [Brown pelican](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brown_pelican) — Pacific Coast native, removed from U.S. endangered species list in 2009

2026-05-02.text:
Spent the afternoon on the Cambria coast before heading inland to Paso Robles for an evening at Sensorio's sweeping light art installation across the dark hillsides.

**Highlights:**

- [Moonstone Beach Park](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moonstone_Beach) — a coastal park in Cambria, CA, known for its driftwood-lined boardwalk and informal folk-art installations along the bluffs
- [Sensorio Field of Light](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bruce_Munro) — outdoor installation by British artist Bruce Munro featuring over 58,000 fiber-optic stems across 15 acres of Paso Robles wine country; opened 2019 and solar-powered

2026-05-03.text:
Drove north along CA-1 after a late brunch, stopping at the McWay Falls overlook in Julia Pfeiffer Burns State Park under overcast skies for a moody, uncrowded midday view.

**Highlights:**
- [McWay Falls](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/McWay_Falls) — an 80-foot tidefall that drops directly onto a secluded cove beach; one of the few such waterfalls on the California coast
- [Julia Pfeiffer Burns State Park](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Julia_Pfeiffer_Burns_State_Park) — established 1962, named after a local Big Sur homesteader; the overlook trail provides the classic vantage point above the cove

2026-04-29.text:
Spent a sunny Wednesday cycling Avila Beach's pier in the morning, then drove south to explore Pismo Beach's sea arches and coastal bluffs in the afternoon.

**Highlights:**

- [Avila Beach Pier](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Avila_Beach,_California) — historic Central Coast harbor pier offering views of the calm Avila Beach anchorage and surrounding coastal hills
- [Pismo Beach](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pismo_Beach,_California) — city on California's Central Coast known for its rugged sea arches, tide pools, and rocky Pacific shoreline
- [Dinosaur Caves Park](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dinosaur_Caves_Park) — coastal bluff park in Pismo Beach named for a former dinosaur-themed attraction, offering panoramic views of sandstone cliffs and tide pools below

2026-04-30.text:
Spent the morning along the Cayucos shoreline examining a graffiti-covered shipwreck visible from the coastal bluffs, then drove south to the hamlet of Harmony for a brief, cheerful roadside stop.

**Highlights:**

- [Cayucos, California](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cayucos,_California) — small Central Coast community incorporated in the 1860s, known for its pier and scenic bluffs along Highway 1
- [Cayucos Pier](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cayucos_Pier) — built in 1875, one of the oldest surviving piers on the California coast
- [Harmony, California](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harmony,_California) — unincorporated community with a population of roughly 18, formerly home to the Harmony Valley Creamery; now a tourist stop with glass blowing, pottery, and wine tasting
